entries.english:
1390, 30 August. Ulrich called Drochowetz of Umlowitz gives Hohenfurt Monastery a half-hide in the village of Suchdol as free property.

CLXXVII. Scripture teaches that we should honor God with our substance and make friends through the mammon of iniquity so that we may be received into the eternal dwellings. Therefore, let present and future generations know that I, Ulrich called Drochowetz of Umlowitz, of my own full and free will, with the goodwill of my lawful wife Jarka and my heirs, have granted and fully conveyed to the monastery of Hohenfurt, for my salvation, that of my parents, predecessors, and successors, half a hide in the village called Suchdol, which Matthias by name cultivates, with full lordship and jurisdiction, rent, and all appurtenances, for perpetual possession. The religious and devout brothers of the Order of Saint Bernard at the aforesaid monastery of Hohenfurt shall remember me and my parents in the canonical hours and their prayers, and shall diligently pray Almighty God for all those named above and for all predecessors and successors who have departed this world. In witness, my seal is attached together with the seal of Lord Heinrich von Rosenberg, who graciously agreed to attach his seal at my request, and the seal of Benessius called Maczuta of Hersslak. Given and done in 1390, on the feast of the holy martyrs Felix and Adauctus.

Three small seals hang from parchment strips: a and c in white wax, b in red. (a) A helmet with horn-shaped crest, seal of Ulrich of Umlowitz. (b) The previously described seal of Lord Heinrich von Rosenberg. (c) Poorly printed, so neither image nor inscription can be identified.

CLXXVIII. 6 January 1394, Rudnicz. Archbishop Johann of Prague grants an indulgence to the collegiate church of Hohenfurt. Johannes, by the grace of God archbishop of Prague and legate of the Apostolic See, to all Christian faithful reborn in the sacred font of baptism, eternal salvation in the Lord. Because the glorious merits of the saints are revered, we, in the office entrusted to us, invite Christ’s faithful all the more willingly when we know this especially concerns their salvation. Wishing that the faithful might visit with fervent devotion each day the chapel of the Blessed Virgin Mary at Hohenfurt Monastery, under the title of Saint Nicholas the Confessor, and receive there spiritual gifts, namely indulgences and remission of sins, and wishing through such gifts to make the faithful acceptable to God, the Virgin Mary, and all the saints, trusting in Almighty God’s mercy and in the merits and intercession of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, we mercifully grant in the Lord forty days’ indulgence from the penances imposed on all who are truly penitent, contrite, and confessed, and who visit that chapel and, kneeling before the altar of Saint Nicholas the Confessor, pray five “Our Fathers” and seven “Hail Marys.” In witness, these letters bear our attached seal. Given at Rudnicz on 6 January 1394.

The seal, in red wax and hanging from a parchment strip, has already been described.

CLXXIX. 9 October 1395, Hohenfurt. The same archbishop grants forty days’ indulgence to those who pray for Lords Peter, Jodok, and Ulrich von Rosenberg, buried in Hohenfurt collegiate church. Johannes, by the grace of God archbishop of Prague and legate of the Apostolic See, to all Christian faithful reborn in the sacred font of baptism, salvation in the Lord. Since it is pious and salutary to pray for the dead, so that those who die in Christ may, through the pious petitions of the faithful, be released from the bonds of their sins, and since the bodies of the noble Lords Peter, Jodok, and Ulrich von Rosenberg rest in certain places and chapels of Hohenfurt Cistercian monastery, wishing to invite the faithful to spiritual gifts through their devout prayers for these souls, we, trusting in Almighty God’s mercy and in the merits and intercession of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, mercifully grant in the Lord forty days’ indulgence from the penances imposed on all who are truly penitent, contrite, and confessed, and who enter the aforesaid monastery, kneel, and devoutly pray five “Our Fathers” and seven “Hail Marys” at any hour of the day for the repose of their souls. In witness, these letters bear our attached seal. Given at Hohenfurt on 9 October 1395.

The seal, hanging from a parchment strip, has already been described.
